We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

The guidance: three steps: 1) sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). 2) Doebner modification to form the α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid). 3) amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine coupling).

Thus retrosynthetic disconnections: target -> break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride) and an aniline (the phenyl with methyl). The sulfonyl chloride attached to second aromatic ring (para to the side chain). So precursor 1: p-toluidine (or 4-methyl aniline) and sulfonyl chloride derived from second aromatic ring bearing the side chain (the unsaturated amide). Actually sulfonamide formation: NS(=O)(=O) attached to aromatic ring (first ring). So disconnection: break N-S bond to give sulfonyl chloride attached to second aromatic ring (aryl sulfonyl chloride) and aniline (first ring). So precursor A: 4-methyl aniline (p-toluidine) SMILES: Cc1ccc(N)cc1. Precursor B: aryl sulfonyl chloride with side chain: c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2 attached to side chain? Wait the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second aromatic ring which also has the side chain (the α,β-unsaturated amide). The target has NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2 with the side chain attached? Actually the side chain is attached to the same aromatic ring as the sulfonyl group. In target, the sulfonyl group is attached to the second aromatic ring, which also bears the side chain at para position? The SMILES: ...NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the sulfonyl group attached to the second ring at position 1, and the side chain (C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N) attached at para position relative to sulfonyl? The SMILES shows c2ccc(/C=C/... )cc2 attached directly to sulfonyl group. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be the same aromatic ring with sulfonyl chloride instead of sulfonamide, and the side chain present (still as unsaturated amide). So we need to generate that via earlier steps.

Second step: Doebner modification forms the α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid from aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid, giving the side chain as /C=C/C(=O)OH (carboxylic acid). Then later amide formation couples with aniline (c3ccccc3N) to give amide. So the side chain after Doebner is unsaturated carboxylic acid attached to aromatic ring (the second ring). Then amide formation attaches an aniline (c3ccccc3N) to form the amide.

Thus retrosynthesis: Target -> break amide bond (C(=O)N) to give unsaturated carboxylic acid (aryl-CH=CH-COOH) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). That's step 3 (amide formation forward). So precursor after step 3: aryl-CH=CH-COOH attached to second aromatic ring with sulfonyl chloride (instead of sulfonamide). So we need to have sulfonyl chloride present already. So step 2: break the double bond formation? Actually Doebner modification forms the α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid. So reverse: we can disconnect the double bond to give aromatic aldehyde (aryl-CHO) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). So precursor after step 2: aromatic aldehyde attached to second aromatic ring (with sulfonyl chloride). So we need aromatic aldehyde with sulfonyl chloride substituent.

Thus overall route:

1) Target -> disconnection of amide: precursors: (a) unsaturated carboxylic acid aryl-CH=CH-COOH with sulfonyl chloride; (b) aniline (c3ccccc3N). Reaction: amide coupling (carboxylic acid + amine) using coupling agent.

2) Unsaturated carboxylic acid precursor -> disconnection of double bond via Doebner: precursors: aromatic aldehyde (aryl-CHO) with sulfonyl chloride; malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). Reaction: Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid).

3) Aromatic aldehyde precursor -> disconnection of sulfonamide: break N-S to give sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride) and aniline (p-toluidine). Reaction: sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride).

Thus we need to retrieve template IDs for each reaction. Use search to find templates for sulfonamide formation, Doebner modification, amide coupling.

Search for sulfonamide formation: functional_groups_broken: primary amines? Actually forward reaction: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide. So broken: primary amines and sulfonyl chloride? The functional groups broken are primary amines and sulfonyl chloride (acyl chloride type). Formed: sulfonamides. Let's search.
